solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In Paris I read about this writer's rejected complaint

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: the word read is put around the next piece, as if surrounding it

parts.note: taken as the word itself, wrapped around the middle

indicators.note: rejected means the piece for this writer's is turned back to front

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: I'm, written IM

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris reads about a writer's turned-down grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer's' is the setter's I'm; 'rejected' turns it round to MI, and 'about' wraps the word read around that.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeremiad is a long mournful lament or list of woes, named after the prophet Jeremiah.

clue.text: Primate crushed by judge's joke

indicators.note: in a down clue, being crushed by something means sitting beneath it, so the judge comes on top

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey squashed under a judge, presented as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or prank.

clue.text: Responsibility quietly removed from uncultured pleb

indicators.note: removed from says that one letter is taken out of the word for the pleb

parts.note: a prole is a member of the common working masses, a pleb
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A duty quietly taken away from a boorish commoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is a function or part one is responsible for playing.

clue.text: Fateful sign all of the French associated with mass

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass
an omen is a sign of things to come
tous is French for all

explanation.surface: A portentous sign in France linked with a Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentous is of great consequence, decisive for what follows.

clue.text: Queen's article on new enemy upset most of intelligent Society

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word for the enemy is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: most of says the final letter of the word for intelligent is dropped

parts.note: clever means intelligent

explanation.surface: A queen is accused of putting an enemy in charge of a clever society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the enemy upside down in this down clue; 'most of' drops the last letter of the word for intelligent. The 's after Queen is a link (is): Anne of Cleves was Henry VIII's fourth wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne of Cleves was the fourth wife of Henry VIII and so an English queen consort.

clue.text: Reckless senior officer's assistant enthralled by chart

indicators.note: being enthralled, held captive, by something places the assistant inside the chart

parts.note: a map is a chart
ADC is aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a general

explanation.surface: A general's aide is spellbound by a map.
explanation.walkthrough: ADC (aide-de-camp) is a military officer who assists a senior commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap person acts impulsively and wildly, without thought for consequences.

clue.text: Trouble-making Greek disrupting a match?

indicators.note: disrupting means the Greek breaks into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: a go is a bout or contest, a match

explanation.surface: A Greek troublemaker interrupting a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive behaviour, hassle or bother.

clue.text: Generous woman taken in by communication about hours

indicators.note: taken in by places the woman inside the rest
about means the communication wraps around the hours

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a communication
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A kind woman absorbed in a message about the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'about' puts hours inside the telegram word, then 'taken in by' slips the woman in after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable people are generous with their giving or in their judgements.

clue.text: Plot French film director takes on in cultivated area

parts.note: to plot is to plan
Jacques Tati directed Monsieur Hulot's Holiday
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French director's scheme to film in a farmed area.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation is an estate where crops such as cotton or tea are grown.

clue.text: Friend o' the compiler's briefly seen with old horse

parts.note: a pal is a friend
the shortened of, standing for O

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the setter's own: mine

explanation.surface: The setter's chum seen beside an elderly horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A palomino is a golden horse with a white mane and tail.

clue.text: Lizard droppings mostly found in Iowa

indicators.note: found in places the shortened droppings within the state abbreviation

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is cut from the word for droppings

parts.note: guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats

explanation.surface: Bird droppings in Iowa turning out to be mostly lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguana is a large tropical American lizard.

clue.text: There's rhyme as well as reason in this jazz style

definitions.text: There's rhyme as well as reason in this jazz style

parts.words: There's rhyme as well as reason in this jazz style
parts.note: the name is a rhyming doubled word, so there is rhyme in it; 'neither rhyme nor reason' is the idiom being played on

explanation.surface: A remark that a jazz style makes sense and rhymes too.
explanation.definitionFit: Boogie-woogie is a fast blues piano style with a rolling bass, its name a rhyming reduplication.

clue.text: Studious type watching the cricket, perhaps?

definitions.text: Studious type watching the cricket, perhaps?

parts.words: Studious type watching the cricket, perhaps?
parts.note: the cricket here is the insect, not the sport, so the scholar watching it studies insects

explanation.surface: A bookish person spectating at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the English bat-and-ball game, but here it is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientists who study insects observe creatures like crickets as part of their work.

clue.text: Hibernian ancestry second husband denied, getting shot!

indicators.note: denied means those letters are refused a place, taken out

parts.note: Hibernian means Irish, and ancestry is descent

explanation.surface: An Irish-descended man shot after a second husband is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot silk shows changing colours as the light moves, which is why 'shot' can define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot fabric shimmers with shifting colours, exactly the play of colours that iridescent describes.

clue.text: Lacking firm evidence, I'm internally no better

indicators.note: internally places the I'm letters inside the word for lacking evidence

parts.note: something unproved lacks firm evidence
written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone admits that without proof they are no better inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has not been enhanced or improved stays no better than before.

clue.text: Piece of litter on doorstep

indicators.note: of signals a part taken out of the words that follow, spanning their letters

explanation.surface: A bit of rubbish left on the front step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of' looks like it picks a fragment, but 'Piece' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical piece with a recurring principal theme.

clue.text: Aware of fellow worker swigging spirit from East

indicators.note: swigging, drinking down, puts the spirit inside the fellow worker

parts.note: CO is short for co-, a fellow or partner
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

indicators.note: from East means the word is read right to left, as from the east side of an across clue

parts.note: zing is spirit or liveliness

explanation.surface: Knowing a colleague downs liquor from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from East' reads the spirit right to left (GNIZ), and 'swigging' has the fellow worker drinking it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cognizant of something means having knowledge or awareness of it.

clue.text: Mimicking cry of kid at play a president's wife's mounted

parts.note: a child playing tag shouts I'm it

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the wife's name climbs upward, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita was Eva Perón, wife of Argentina's President Juan Perón

explanation.surface: A child at play copying the president's wife climbing on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitative behaviour copies or mimics something else.

clue.text: A commotion connected with mother's inlaid work

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a scene is a public fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A fuss made about Mum's inlay.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene work is metal inlaid with gold or silver, as in Damascus steel.

clue.text: I see nothing grand in this dome-shaped dwelling

indicators.note: in places the grand inside the other letters

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
O is the round figure zero
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone sees nothing grand inside an igloo.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit snow houses are built as domes of packed snow blocks.

clue.text: Start of rally with state soldier, perhaps

parts.note: in tennis a rally begins with a serve, the service
Oman is a state on the Arabian Peninsula

explanation.surface: Kick off a political rally with a soldier from the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of rally' looks like an instruction to take R, but it is the tennis service that starts a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: A female soldier is one example of a member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Visionary declaration of banker at table?

definitions.meaning: visionary means perfect but existing only as an idea
the card dealer, the bank at a gaming table, announces that he will deal

explanation.surface: A dreamer's announcement while running a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal and visionary both describe something perfect yet imagined; read as two words it is the dealer's 'I deal'.

clue.text: Asian desert, one with marshland up to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up to the north means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a bog is marshland

explanation.surface: An Asian desert with a marsh to its north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a large desert in Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Alignment required to make washing-up place sound?

indicators.note: sound says the word is to be heard, pronounced aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: the dishes are washed up in a kitchen sink

explanation.surface: Asking whether a kitchen sink needs straightening to be sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning sturdy, but it is the signal for a word heard aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in sync means being synchronised, aligned in timing.

clue.text: Was jealous of girl embraced by English chap

indicators.note: embraced by puts the girl inside the Englishman

parts.note: Ned is a man's name, a chap
Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: Someone felt envious of a girl being hugged by an English bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: To envy someone is to resent their good fortune, being jealous of them.

clue.text: A ghastly start for one city plant!

parts.note: grim means ghastly or horrible

indicators.note: start for means taking only the opening letter of the word one

parts.note: NY is New York City

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a horrible beginning for a single urban plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a wildflower of the rose family with yellow flower spikes.

clue.text: Divine in church vestment, not the first to walk unsteadily

indicators.note: in puts the divine inside the shortened vestment
not the first says the opening letter is dropped from the word for the vestment

parts.note: a stole is a scarf-like vestment worn by clergy
DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine

explanation.surface: A clergyman in his vestment, toddling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' beheads the vestment (TOLE), and 'in' puts the Doctor of Divinity inside. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short unsteady steps, like a young child.

clue.text: Rosalind's ally caught eating last of the summer veg

indicators.note: eating puts those letters inside the ally and the caught

parts.note: Celia is Rosalind's cousin and companion in Shakespeare's As You Like It

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean companion caught eating end-of-summer vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes E and R from 'the summer'; 'eating' puts them inside CELIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeriac is a root vegetable, a variety of celery grown for its swollen base.
